data.name: Heroes Rise: HeroFall
data.detailed_description:
Would a hero like you assassinate the president of the United States to defend the right to be Powered?

As the corrupt President Victon launches his oppressive campaign of Powered Regulation, your Legendary heroic rise transforms into something much more: you must become a political icon fighting to restore Powered rights in America. This new battle takes a twisted turn when your once-greatest enemy, Prodigal, tells you President Victon’s darkest secret....

Now you are faced with the biggest choices of your career: Do you trust the word of your archenemy? Will you evade President Victon's gang of criminal bounty hunters? Can you save your family and complete your rise as a Legendary hero?

"Heroes Rise: HeroFall" completes the epic Heroes Rise trilogy by Zachary Sergi, featuring the smash hits "Heroes Rise: The Prodigy" and "Heroes Rise: The Hero Project," interactive novels where your choices control the story. The Heroes Rise trilogy is entirely text-based—without graphics or sound effects—and driven by the vast, unstoppable power of your imagination.

All of your decisions lead to this epic conclusion, where you must truly define what you believe is right and what you stand for as a hero—and what (or whom) you’re willing to sacrifice for those ideals. Play as male or female, gay or straight, and decide how your story will end. How many alternate endings can you unlock?

How High Will You Rise?


  • Over 118,000 words
  • Play as gay or straight, male or female
  • Five possible romance options
  • Save your parents from the Devoid prison for Powered criminals
  • Unleash your mysterious "Infini" powers

reviews.review:
[h1]SUNK COST FALLACY[/h1]

As a big fan of games in the Interactive Fiction genre, I usually try my best not to be too harsh on them. They are often written by a single person working on them as a hobby, so I don't expect AAA-quality writing. Unfortunately, when it comes to the Heroes Rise trilogy, I've seen it recommended many times as an introduction to the genre, or at least as one of the "better" series out there. I'm sorry, but I just don't see it. 
I know people can have different tastes, but Heroes Rise as a whole is simply not good. It's a very rushed, generic story about heroes and villains that doesn't do anything particularly well. Recommending it to new readers would be a disservice to the genre.
I wouldn't have even played HeroFall if I'd known better beforehand, but I'd already finished the two previous games. That's when the sunk cost fallacy kicked in, and I decided to see the story through to the end. 
Was it worth it? No. I didn't see any improvement in any aspect of the game, and simply stumbled my way to the ending. At least it didn't take too long to get there, since you can finish HeroFall in less than four hours.
[b]I can't recommend HeroFall, nor can I recommend the rest of the series.[/b] It's just not good, to put it mildly.

[b]Story[/b]
It's a direct continuation of The Hero Project. Prodigy is back, and you're on a mission to stop the evil president from doing whatever he wants.
The story is just so stupid at times that I don't even want to bother describing everything that happens. At least your choices from the previous two games matter here to some extent, affecting who you see and how they react to you, so that's a plus.
The rushed pacing also completely kills the plot for me. The entire Heroes Rise trilogy is fast-paced by definition, but here the pacing somehow feels even faster than before. You're constantly thrown from one thing to another without anything having enough time to feel important. This makes the ending especially unsatisfying, as the entire story wraps up in a single chapter.
Similarly to The Hero Project, the story has plenty of moments where it tries to be overly preachy. This isn't necessarily a problem when the writer knows how to handle it, but here it often detracts from the plot. Like, I know some things are morally wrong, so, game, can you please stop lecturing me about it?

[b]Characters[/b]
All of the side characters, with the possible exception of Prodigal, are completely irrelevant and feel like they're only here for the sake of being here. They exist mostly to push the plot forward and then show up in the final battle. Beyond that, they barely matter.
The romance is also here just for the sake of having a romance, without any meaningful buildup. Barely after starting the game, I'm already given an option like, "The bond I feel with Prodigal might be more than just one of friendship." You couldn't start a romance path in a worse way if you tried. It's so fucking dumb and rushed that I genuinely felt insulted seeing something like this. If you can't be bothered to write a decent romance plot, then don't give the player the option in the first place. Just leave it out.

[b]Audio & Visuals[/b]
This game is purely text-based, so there’s not much to comment on in terms of audio or visuals. Still, I’ll leave my usual note for interactive fiction: even basic visuals and audio could make these games more accessible and appealing to a wider audience, similar to what Roadwarden or Wayfarer have done.

[b]Technicalities[/b]
The lack of a save system - or at least a "back to the previous page" button - is just incredibly frustrating. I can’t stress enough how much I dislike it when interactive fiction games do this. It’s all too easy to misclick on a choice you didn’t intend, especially in longer games, so give players a way to fix it.
I didn't notice any bugs, typos, or other issues.
